description: A single-panel bright-field transmission electron micrograph of deformed Fe–35% Al, showing dislocation substructure within one large grain. Dark, curved and mostly elongated dislocation segments and short dipole segments lie against a lighter matrix, with the majority of lines appearing straight or gently bowed rather than tangled. The upper-left and central regions contain the highest density of dark segments, some forming pairs/loops characteristic of dipole segments; the lower half of the field is noticeably more uniform with a faint mottled, banded contrast. In the lower-right corner an arrow marks the imaging vector, and the caption identifies it as [1 1 0]. No crystallographic reflection, pattern, or diffraction spots are drawn on the panel; the caption states the zone axis is near [1 1 3]. A scale bar printed as 0.25µm sits in the bottom-right. No numeric magnification, axis, or data values are printed. Taken as one image, the panel demonstrates dislocations (identified in the citing text as B2 superdislocations composed of two (1/2)[1 1 1] partials) together with weak remnant background fringes, interpreted as evidence that their movement destroys some DO3 order.

observations.observation: The figure is a single bright-field TEM micrograph of deformed Fe–35% Al showing dark dislocation segments in a lighter matrix.
A scale bar in the bottom-right corner is printed as 0.25µm.
A black arrow in the lower-right marks the imaging vector, which the caption identifies as [1 1 0].
The caption states the zone axis is near [1 1 3].
Dark, elongated, mostly straight or gently bowed dislocation segments and paired/dipole segments are concentrated in the upper-left and central regions of the field.
The lower half of the micrograph shows a more uniform, faint mottled/banded contrast interpreted as weak remnant background fringes.
The citing text identifies the dislocations as superdislocations of the B2 lattice, constituted by two partials of Burgers vector (1/2)[1 1 1] each.
The citing text states that movement of these superdislocations destroys some of the DO3 order, indicated by the weak remnant fringes seen in this figure.
No numeric magnification, axis labels, or quantitative data values are printed on the panel; the only printed numeric value is the 0.25µm scale bar.
